Janus effect

Source: R/voe.R
janus.Rd

Computes the definitions of the Janus effect used in the vibration of effects literature. The Janus effect indicates that the same association changes direction across specifications.

Usage

janus(x, ...)

# Default S3 method
janus(x, p = NULL, q = c(0.01, 0.99), null = 0, alpha = 0.05, ...)

# S3 method for class 'pima'
janus(
  x,
  focal = NULL,
  p.adjusted = NULL,
  q = c(0.01, 0.99),
  alpha = 0.05,
  which.response = NULL,
  xvar = "estimate",
  focal.var = NULL,
  p = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'pima.multi'
janus(
  x,
  focal = NULL,
  p.adjusted = NULL,
  q = c(0.01, 0.99),
  alpha = 0.05,
  which.response = NULL,
  xvar = "estimate",
  focal.var = NULL,
  p = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'list'
janus(
  x,
  focal = NULL,
  p.adjusted = NULL,
  q = c(0.01, 0.99),
  alpha = 0.05,
  which.response = NULL,
  xvar = "estimate",
  focal.var = NULL,
  p = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
janus(
  x,
  focal = NULL,
  p.adjusted = NULL,
  q = c(0.01, 0.99),
  alpha = 0.05,
  which.response = NULL,
  xvar = "estimate",
  focal.var = NULL,
  p = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

a numeric vector of estimates, a pima object, a pima.multi object created with fit.specs, a list of fitted lm or glm models, or a table returned by spec_table().

...

further arguments (currently unused).

p

for vectors, a numeric vector of p-values, same length as x (if NULL, J_sig and J_ext are NA). Otherwise, the column of p-values of the specification table, as in spec_curve().

q

probabilities; only the extremes are used.

null

value under the null hypothesis (0 on the link scale).

alpha

significance level.

focal, focal.var

coefficients and variables to consider, as in spec_curve(); by default the tested coefficients (pima), the focal predictors (pima.multi) or all the coefficients except the intercept.

p.adjusted

which p-values to use, with the same rules as spec_curve(): adjusted p-values only exist for pima objects analysed with a correction. Published values in the literature use raw p-values.

which.response

responses to consider; defaults to all.

xvar

column of the specification table whose sign is used. Any column with the same sign as the coefficient (estimate, pcor, wald.t) gives the same result.

Value

For vectors, a list with J_range, J_pct, J_ext, J_sig, J_frac. Otherwise, a data frame with one row per response x coefficient.

Details

Let \(x_1, \dots, x_M\) be the estimates of the \(M\) specifications, \(p_s\) their p-values, \(\theta_0\) the value under the null (null), \(Q_q\) the \(q\)-th quantile across the specifications (interpolated, as in stats::quantile()) and \(q_1 < q_2\) the extremes of q.

  • J_range (Vinatier et al. 2025) : minimum and maximum estimates on opposite sides of the null, \(\min_s x_s < \theta_0 < \max_s x_s\).

  • J_pct (Patel et al. 2015; Palpacuer et al. 2019; Vinatier et al. 2024) : extreme quantiles on opposite sides of the null, \(Q_{q_1}(x) < \theta_0 < Q_{q_2}(x)\).

  • J_ext (Vinatier et al. 2024) : the specifications \(s_1\) and \(s_2\) closest to \(Q_{q_1}(x)\) and \(Q_{q_2}(x)\) are on opposite sides of the null and both significant, \(x_{s_1} < \theta_0 < x_{s_2}\) and \(p_{s_1}, p_{s_2} \le \alpha\).

  • J_sig (Klau et al. 2021; Klau et al. 2023) : at least one significant estimate in each direction, i.e. there are \(s\) and \(s'\) with \(p_s, p_{s'} \le \alpha\) and \(x_s < \theta_0 < x_{s'}\).

  • J_frac (Tierney et al. 2021) : proportion of estimates greater than the null, \(\frac{1}{M} \sum_{s=1}^{M} \mathbf{1}(x_s > \theta_0)\).

References

Klau S, Hoffmann S, Patel CJ, Ioannidis JPA, Boulesteix A (2021). “Examining the Robustness of Observational Associations to Model, Measurement and Sampling Uncertainty with the Vibration of Effects Framework.” International Journal of Epidemiology, 50(1), 266–278. doi:10.1093/ije/dyaa164 .

Klau S, Schönbrodt FD, Patel CJ, Ioannidis JPA, Boulesteix A, Hoffmann S (2023). “Comparing the Vibration of Effects due to Model, Data Pre-Processing and Sampling Uncertainty on a Large Data Set in Personality Psychology.” Meta-Psychology, 7. doi:10.15626/MP.2020.2556 .

Palpacuer C, Hammas K, Duprez R, Laviolle B, Ioannidis JPA, Naudet F (2019). “Vibration of Effects from Diverse Inclusion/Exclusion Criteria and Analytical Choices: 9216 Different Ways to Perform an Indirect Comparison Meta-Analysis.” BMC Medicine, 17(1), 174. doi:10.1186/s12916-019-1409-3 .

Patel CJ, Burford B, Ioannidis JPA (2015). “Assessment of Vibration of Effects due to Model Specification Can Demonstrate the Instability of Observational Associations.” Journal of Clinical Epidemiology, 68(9), 1046–1058. doi:10.1016/j.jclinepi.2015.05.029 .

Tierney BT, Anderson E, Tan Y, Claypool K, Tangirala S, Kostic AD, Manrai AK, Patel CJ (2021). “Leveraging Vibration of Effects Analysis for Robust Discovery in Observational Biomedical Data Science.” PLOS Biology, 19(9), e3001398. doi:10.1371/journal.pbio.3001398 .

Vinatier C, Hoffmann S, Patel C, DeVito NJ, Cristea IA, Tierney B, Ioannidis JPA, Naudet F (2025). “What Is the Vibration of Effects?” BMJ Evidence-Based Medicine, 30(1), 61–65. doi:10.1136/bmjebm-2023-112747 .

Vinatier C, Palpacuer C, Scanff A, Naudet F (2024). “Vibration of Effects Resulting from Treatment Selection in Mixed-Treatment Comparisons: A Multiverse Analysis on Network Meta-Analyses of Antidepressants in Major Depressive Disorder.” BMJ Evidence-Based Medicine, 29(5), 324–332. doi:10.1136/bmjebm-2024-112848 .

See also

Other vibration of effects: voe(), voe_variance(), volcano()

Examples

# vectors of estimates and p-values
set.seed(1)
est <- rnorm(100, mean = 0.1, sd = 0.2)
p <- runif(100)
janus(est, p)
#> $J_range
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $J_pct
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $J_ext
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $J_sig
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $J_frac
#> [1] 0.75
#> 

# a multiverse of fitted models
multi <- create_multi(
  Sepal.Width ~ Sepal.Length + Petal.Width + Species,
  data = iris,
  focal = "Sepal.Length",
  nfuns = "log",
  fit.specs = list(lm = lm)
)
janus(multi)
#>      response  coefficient n_spec J_range J_pct J_ext J_sig    J_frac
#> 1 Sepal.Width Sepal.Length      6    TRUE  TRUE FALSE FALSE 0.8333333
